content: It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug. The active metabolite of ozanimod inhibits MAO-B in vitro, which can lead to serious adverse reactions, including hypertensive crisis. Therefore, coadministration of ozanimod with drugs that increase norepinephrine or serotonin is not recommended. Both eliglustat and ozanimod prolong the QTc interval. It is advised to avoid or use an alternative drug. Eltrombopag increases the toxicity of ozanimod through other mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Eluxadoline also increases the toxicity of ozanimod through similar mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Enasidenib increases the levels or effects of ozanimod through other mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Enasidenib, a sensitive OATP1B1, OATP1B3, or BCRP substrate, may lead to serious toxicities with minimal concentration changes. If unavoidable, reduce the substrate dosage as per prescribing information. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ozanimod decreases the efficacy of live-attenuated vaccines, such as the influenza virus vaccine (quadrivalent and trivalent intranasal), measles-mumps-rubella vaccine, and measles-mumps-rubella-varicella vaccine, due to its immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid live-attenuated vaccines during ozanimod treatment and for up to 3 months after discontinuation. Both ozanimod and drugs like isoflurane, itraconazole, and mirtazapine prolong the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ketoconazole, lapatinib, leniolisib, and levoketoconazole increase the toxicity of ozanimod through other mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Lasmitidan increases the toxicity of ozanimod through other mechanisms, and ozanimod increases the toxicity of lasmitidan by sympathetic effects. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Fosphenytoin decreases the levels or effects of ozanimod through other mechanisms. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Ozanimod decreases the efficacy of the influenza virus vaccine (intranasal), measles-mumps-rubella vaccine, and other live-attenuated vaccines due to its immunosuppressive effects, increasing the risk of infection. Avoid live-attenuated vaccines during ozanimod treatment and for up to 3 months after discontinuation. In summary, ozanimod interacts with numerous drugs, often increasing toxicity through sympathetic (adrenergic) effects or by altering the metabolism of its active metabolites. These interactions can lead to serious adverse effects, including hypertensive crisis, QTc prolongation, or reduced efficacy of live-attenuated vaccines. It is crucial to avoid or use alternative drugs in these cases and monitor for hypertension during concomitant use.
